《Bees vs Zombees》是Deadpixel开发并发行的一款像素风格游戏，其包含了肉鸽、塔防、RTS等要素，尽管这些要素看起来有些不匹配，但玩起来却意外地有趣。游戏提供了10张地图（大关卡）供玩家游玩，每个大关卡含有十几到数十个小关卡（根据难度而变化），玩家通过各个小关卡以获得全局buff，再通过击杀boss以通关一个大关卡。 这游戏的剧情十分简单粗暴，有一些蜜蜂变成了僵尸蜜蜂，玩家需要指挥正常的蜜蜂抵御僵尸蜜蜂的攻击，保卫自己的蜂巢以及蜂后，同时收复被僵尸蜜蜂占领的失地。 相比剧情的贫瘠，这款游戏的玩法倒是令人眼前一亮。玩家选择一张地图（大关卡，有3种不同难度），再从10位蜂后以及10位蜜蜂工匠中各选一位开始闯关，不同的蜂后有不同的全局buff和技能，不同的工匠除了有不同的全局buff，还决定了本局游戏可以使用的防御塔类型。游戏地图是六边形网格地图，玩家开局在一个格子上，地图BOSS在远离玩家的另一个格子上，玩家和BOSS之间会有很多小怪（其中一些是精英怪）阻挡玩家，玩家可以移动到小怪所在的格子进入小关卡。小关卡是一场兼具塔防和RTS要素的短时间战斗，玩家开局具有一定数量的蜂蜜以及一个需要保卫的蜂巢，僵尸蜜蜂会从蜂巢两侧源源不断地进攻，消耗蜂蜜可以放置防御塔、升级防御塔、给防御塔安装升级组件、释放法术，消灭足够数量的僵尸蜜蜂就能通过小关卡。当玩家通过一个小关卡后就能获得一项全局buff，一路收集全局buff并打赢地图boss就能通过大关卡。游戏共有43种不同的全局buff，精英怪小关卡会掉落效果更强的全局buff（紫色背景）。玩家没打赢小关卡也不会直接game over，大关卡总共有3条命，可以失败3次。 这款游戏的难度中等偏上，对于没玩过塔防和RTS游戏的玩家来说可能会有些难以上手。这里推荐游戏开局打完新手教程后直接认输一次，这样能解锁僵尸女王。僵尸女王没有蜂蜜这种设计，改用蜂巢血量进行放置、升级防御塔等相关操作，相当于在小关卡的开局就能获得一座升满级、装满升级组件的防御塔（推荐攻击范围无限大的迫击炮）以及一些低级防御塔，前期的非精英怪小关卡可以用这种方法无脑乱杀。此外，不同于大多数肉鸽游戏只能从多条路线里选择一条通往boss的路线，这游戏可以打完地图上所有小关卡，尽可能拿完buff，攒一身神装再挑战boss。虽然玩家在地图上逗留太久就会刷僵尸蜜蜂追兵来追杀玩家，但是当追兵的位置刚好在玩家旁边时可以直接移动过去无伤吃掉追兵，因此这个追兵机制几乎不影响玩家清完全部小怪再打boss。 这款游戏有一些奇怪的缺点，游戏支持切换全屏/窗口化模式，但是窗口化模式下无法调节分辨率，在视觉效果上全屏和窗口化是没有区别的。当玩家进入一个大关卡后，要么一口气通关整个大关卡，要么直接失败，没有中途保存以便下次启动游戏继续战斗的选项。总的来说这是两个非常奇怪的缺点，虽然对游戏体验的影响不是很大，但这不像是2024年的游戏会有的缺点。 总的来说，《Bees vs Zombees》是一款质量优秀、价格合理、玩法新颖的肉鸽+RTS+塔防游戏，推荐喜欢这些游戏类型的玩家入手。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45519015/]“无趣评测”[/url][/td][/table]

《Bees vs Zombees》是一部像素风格的肉鸽塔防游戏，游戏主角是各种勤劳的蜜蜂，为我们带来一场保卫蜂巢的塔防守护战，乐趣满满。 游戏玩法很简单，玩过保卫萝卜吧，那就会玩这个了。首先进入关卡，选择难度，然后选择角色。保卫萝卜的核心是萝卜，那保卫蜂巢的核心，不容置疑的是峰后，所以在几种峰后里面选一个。不过，与保卫萝卜有一些不一样，保卫萝卜不需要牛马来建造塔防，保卫蜂巢需要牛马来建造塔防，所以再选一个工蜂。为什么选工蜂呢？因为要选。 蜂后和工蜂多种选择，就意味着他们的技能是多种多样的，所以看清楚效果，合理选择搭配，然后就可以开始一场快乐的游戏了。 游戏的塔防模式也比较有特色，以横版2d视角来展示，敌人从两侧进入，向着地图中间蜂巢，而我们可以在蜂巢周围建造各种小防御塔，来防御敌人的进攻。不同的防御塔，配合不同的摆设角度，往往有不同的奇效。而在大boss登场的时候，会给一个特写，告诉我们最后的敌人来了，快干死他。 游戏肉鸽的模式，决定了玩法的多种性，每一把的游戏都充满着乐趣，毕竟不同的搭配，配合不同的加成，构建出的防御战线，往往有不同的效果。可能会闪电五连鞭的光污染，也可能是漫天火海的视觉奇观，那种火力覆盖的感觉，还是比较享受的。 [h1]总结[/h1] 游戏整体来讲还是很不错的，可爱的卡通像素画风，打击感拉满的特效，动态的地图演示，别出心裁的boss展示界面，无一不说明游戏制作的用心，可谓是细节满满。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45519015/]“无趣评测”[/url][/td][/table]

A trainwreck of BEEzare proportions. I don’t know if it’s always been like this, but the current version of the game is a buggy mess (no pun intended this time around). The unlock requirements for the Artisans don’t match the actual actions. Half of the Artisan skills and roughly 30% of the turret cards don’t work. A map has a high chance of freezing on you mid-playthrough, leaving you twiddling your thumbs and doing nothing. Likewise, the mobs can bug out, causing them to run back and forth like a bunch of headless chickens. If it weren’t for all of the above, the game could have been enjoyable and semi-memorable. A case of wasted potential and creator neglect, to be sure.

2025/12/19 review update Considering that the game features enemies with extremely long attack ranges, there are currently only two optimal ways to deal with them: Choosing the 2-cost Queen Bee that can deploy defensive structures. Obtaining the ability that reduces enemy attack range as a reward in the first two or three stages. If neither of these conditions is met, encountering such enemies often results in instantly losing three hearts. Overall, the game’s depth is still insufficient at its current stage, and not every build or combination has a viable chance to clear the game. It is recommended to add meta-progression systems—for example, giving each Queen Bee an independent skill tree, where players earn experience based on their game score and spend it on upgrades. 2025/12/18 The game’s visuals and the variety of starting hero combinations are diverse and engaging. However, there is room for improvement in several areas: UI font readability: The current UI fonts are difficult to read. It is recommended to provide two or three font options for each language. Limited meta-progression: Adding a small amount of out-of-run progression—such as increasing maximum health or allowing additional reroll attempts when selecting abilities—would help make the gameplay experience smoother. Stages are too short: It is recommended that each stage include at least two bosses. The strength of the mid-stage boss could be reduced by around 30%. At present, the game often ends just as a build fully comes together, which feels unfortunate from an overall experience perspective.

Bees vs Zombees is a lively and inventive indie strategy game developed by Deadpixel and published by Nuntius Games and Vsoo Games that blends classic tower defense foundations with roguelike progression and a playful, pun-filled presentation. From the outset, the game makes its tone clear: this is a colorful, fast-moving defense experience where charm and strategy coexist, and where players are tasked with protecting their hive from relentless waves of zombified bees during a tongue-in-cheek apocalypse. Beneath its humorous exterior lies a surprisingly robust tactical framework that rewards planning, adaptability, and experimentation across repeated runs. The core gameplay revolves around defending your hive by selecting a Queen Bee and pairing her with an Artisan, a combination that defines your overall strategy for each run. Each Queen brings unique abilities that influence how you approach combat, whether by empowering allies, directly damaging enemies, or manipulating the battlefield in subtle ways. Artisans, on the other hand, determine the types of towers and defensive structures you can construct, shaping how you control space and manage incoming swarms. The interaction between these two roles creates a strong sense of identity for each run, as different pairings encourage vastly different playstyles and tactical priorities. Runs unfold across procedurally generated maps, ensuring that no two sessions feel exactly alike. Terrain layout, enemy paths, and wave compositions all vary, forcing players to react rather than rely on a single optimal setup. Zombee enemies themselves come in multiple varieties, each introducing specific threats that must be countered through clever tower placement, timely ability use, or strategic spell deployment. This constant pressure keeps the pace brisk and prevents the game from becoming a passive defense exercise, instead demanding ongoing attention and adjustment as conditions evolve. Roguelike elements are deeply integrated into the experience. Between and during waves, players acquire spells, accessories, and upgrades presented in card-like selections that allow for build customization and synergy hunting. These choices can dramatically alter how a run plays out, sometimes turning a struggling defense into an overwhelming force or, conversely, encouraging risky strategies that may pay off spectacularly or fail disastrously. The joy of discovery—finding combinations that unexpectedly complement one another—is a major driver of replayability and keeps experimentation at the heart of the game. Visually, Bees vs Zombees adopts a vibrant pixel art style that emphasizes clarity and personality. Units, towers, and effects are easy to read even during chaotic moments, which is essential in a game where split-second decisions can determine success or failure. The art direction leans heavily into humor, with expressive animations and visual jokes scattered throughout the interface and environments. This lighthearted approach helps offset the intensity of the gameplay, making even repeated defeats feel more encouraging than discouraging. The pacing strikes a balance between accessibility and challenge. Early runs introduce mechanics gradually, allowing new players to grasp the fundamentals without being overwhelmed, while later stages ramp up complexity and difficulty in ways that test mastery of systems and synergies. Failure is an expected and even celebrated part of progression, as each loss provides insight that informs the next attempt. This loop of trial, learning, and refinement is central to the game’s appeal and gives victories a genuine sense of accomplishment. While the scope of the game is relatively compact compared to large-scale strategy titles, this focus works in its favor. Sessions feel tight and purposeful rather than bloated, though some players may wish for additional Queens, Artisans, or enemy types once they’ve spent significant time mastering the existing content. These desires tend to stem from enjoyment of the core mechanics rather than dissatisfaction, highlighting how engaging the foundation already is. Overall, Bees vs Zombees succeeds as a charming and thoughtfully designed fusion of tower defense and roguelike systems. It offers depth without sacrificing approachability, humor without undermining strategy, and replayability without relying on excessive complexity. For players who enjoy tactical planning, build experimentation, and games that encourage learning through iteration, it provides a satisfying and energetic experience that stands out within the indie strategy space. Rating: 8/10

BvZ is a funny and cute little tower defence game that is close to being a fantastic one, but it needs more bug fixing, balancing and some quality of life options to reach its full potential. It uses roguelike/lite elements in a unique way in that the flowers/cards reset and they are random every time, but you get to select a biome, queen and artisan from the beginning. The last two affect the passives, active skills and turrets you get to use. You gradually unlock more options by doing specific things and completing biomes. The game’s style is on point, it’s expressive, recognisable and colourful. The music is the highlight with upbeat and catchy tunes. The game is hilarious with the artisans/queens you get to play with and the wordplay related to bees. The biomes are varied in looks and sometimes they have cool little unique gameplay gimmicks. The turrets and spell cards are satisfying to see in motion. The gameplay can be so fun at the best of times. In terms of flaws, it’s going to be easier to show a list: -Bug fixes. The game has a very nasty one where enemies don’t appear sometimes, ruining your entire run because you can’t save within biomes. This happened a couple of times. Other bugs include the sound suddenly disappearing, starting dialogues getting repeated a second time (in a few biomes) and possibly 3 achievements not unlocking. I’m not 100% certain about the 3 achievements but someone reported not getting the achievement for clearing all biomes on hard. I did not get the achievement for defeating BeeLoki or unlocking the artisan that requires spending 1000 honey even though I completed all the biomes and some multiple times. There is no way for me to check my progress for the achievements, hence me not being certain. -Balance. The balance in ‘Falling Leaves’ biome is the worst for being forced to get into high level fights early due to the narrow path, even on the easiest difficulty. Although it’s the worst, the other last biomes are not great either. Only certain combinations become truly viable. There are clearly losers and winners with the queens and artisans. -QoL options. I don’t understand why you can’t save your run to continue later since a run can take up to an hour if you want to do things thoroughly. Its absence is devastating with the bug that forces you to quit runs. Next, the game only has speed increase during waves but no pause to think things through. This discourages strategy and invites chaos. One minute everything is fine, the next you can lose it all quickly. And lastly, I don’t like being forced to clear easy and normal difficulty to get to the hard difficulty for the achievement. Either give us all the difficulty options from the start or only make easy required to unlock both normal and hard at the same time. I don’t feel like grinding to unlock hard especially with all the bugs and balance issues the game has. It has been hard deciding on whether the game deserves an up- or downvote. There are times where I had lots of fun with BvZ. The game is clearly made with lots of passion and creativity. But other times it frustrates and it feels like such a shame because the game only needs a small push to fix most of the issues. Ultimately, I decided on a downvote in the hope I can change my score once the game receives its much needed update. I’ve spent 15 hours to finish all the biomes while missing 3 achievements. I would love to continue to get the rest of the achievements in the future, when the game is more polished. Edit: A kind member told me where to find BeeLoki. He shows up in the thunder biome but only on hard. I went back to get that achievement. Now I have 2 achievements left (spend 1000 honey and beat all levels on hard). I'm not certain if those are bugged or not.

Really good idea for a Tower Defense game with roguelike mechanics. Sadly, it becomes quite repetitive pretty fast and there are some balancing issues. One character can single handedly win even the hardest of fights very early on, while the others require quite a lot of skill juggling and upgrades farming. Decent game to get on sale if you want some lightweight TD game for an evenging or two.

中规中矩的小品RL，地图两侧出兵纯拼防御塔的机制外加大半是纯数值的升级卡和群伤卡实在算不上内容丰富。人物多到可以拆成女皇和顾问但变数实在不多，女皇的特性基本还是围绕防御塔的数值加加减减，顾问则主要决定防御塔的种类。地图惯例换皮换小机制不过也不强求，优点是可以清全图拿满BUFF再打BOSS，核心BUFF相当好拿所以总体难度不高。 游玩推荐毛子（解锁只需单局不开箱）配孙武或达芬奇，毛子的塔两费一个，别家拍一她拍仨。缺点是防御塔不能常规升级，但只要抽出全塔自动升二的BUFF直接通关。既不需要群伤也不需要升级打起来省心省力，不管对面什么搭配进去无脑城市化，要塞盖完直接赢。 孙武的被动是塔的数量越多攻速越快，但小孙的防御塔种类实在差点意思。达芬奇有全部防御塔可选但被动跟没有一样，两者可以换着玩。 额外的：头一次看见能把BUFF抽干净的RL，爽是挺爽但终局明显没上心。
